description: Canonical Grade 6 math standards registry (2025 Maryland MCCRS codes, re-coded from CCSS via data/standards-crosswalk-2025.json; oldId/consolidatedFrom record each entry's 2010 predecessors) — single source of truth for standard codes, their domain/cluster/topic labels, and the curriculum unit each standard maps to. Generators and audits look standards up here instead of using ad-hoc string heuristics. Keyed by the exact `standard` string used in lessons/*/config.json. Also carries the MPP practice standards and the Grade 5 review standards used by the book's Unit 1 and Unit 10 'Math Is...' lessons, which are review and practice targets rather than Grade 6 instruction.

6.AT.1.fullText: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities.

6.AT.2.fullText: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0, and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship.

6.AT.3.fullText: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

6.AT.3a.fullText: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole-number measurements, find missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane.

6.AT.4.fullText: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100; solve problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the percent.

6.AT.3c.fullText: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units; manipulate and transform units appropriately when multiplying or dividing quantities.

6.NOS.1.fullText: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions, and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions.

6.NOS.2.fullText: Fluently divide multi-digit numbers using the standard algorithm.

6.NOS.3.fullText: Fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm for each operation.

6.NOS.4.fullText: Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers ≤ 100 and the least common multiple of two whole numbers ≤ 12. Use the distributive property to express a sum of two whole numbers with a common factor.

6.NOS.6.fullText: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line; extend number line diagrams and coordinate axes to represent points with negative number coordinates.

6.NOS.7.fullText: Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants of the coordinate plane; recognize that ordered pairs differing only by signs are reflections across one or both axes.

6.NOS.8.fullText: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.

6.NOS.9.fullText: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane; use coordinates and absolute value to find distances.

6.AT.5.fullText: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.

6.AT.6a.fullText: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers.

6.AT.6c.fullText: Evaluate expressions at specific values of their variables, including expressions that arise from formulas used in real-world problems.

6.AT.7.fullText: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

6.AT.8.fullText: Understand solving an equation or inequality as a process of answering which values make it true; use substitution to determine whether a given number makes an equation or inequality true.

6.AT.9.fullText: Write an inequality of the form x > c or x < c to represent a constraint or condition; recognize that such inequalities have infinitely many solutions; represent solutions on number line diagrams.

6.AT.11.fullText: Use variables to represent two quantities in a real-world problem that change in relationship to one another; write an equation to express one quantity, thought of as the dependent variable, in terms of the other quantity, thought of as the independent variable. Analyze the relationship between the dependent and independent variables using graphs and tables, and relate these to the equation.

6.GR.1.fullText: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles and other shapes.

6.GR.2.fullText: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths; apply the formulas V = l·w·h and V = b·h to find volumes of right rectangular prisms.

6.GR.4.fullText: Represent three-dimensional figures using nets made up of rectangles and triangles, and use the nets to find the surface area of these figures.

6.DS.1.fullText: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers.

6.DS.3.fullText: Understand that a set of data collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution which can be described by its center, spread, and overall shape.

6.DS.4.fullText: Recognize that a measure of center for a numerical data set summarizes all of its values with a single number, while a measure of variation describes how its values vary with a single number.

6.DS.5.fullText: Display numerical data in plots on a number line, including dot plots, histograms, and box plots.

6.DS.6c.fullText: Summarize numerical data sets by giving quantitative measures of center (median and/or mean) and variability (interquartile range and/or mean absolute deviation).

6.DS.6d.fullText: Relate the choice of measures of center and variability to the shape of the data distribution and the context in which the data were gathered.

MPP.3.fullText: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

MPP.7.shortLabel: Look For and Make Use of Structure
MPP.7.fullText: Look for and make use of structure.

5.NF.B.4.fullText: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.

5.NBT.B.7.fullText: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths.

5.G.A.2.shortLabel: Graph Points in Quadrant I (Gr 5 review)
5.G.A.2.fullText: Represent real world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.

5.MD.A.1.fullText: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system.

5.MD.C.5.shortLabel: Volume of Right Rectangular Prisms (Gr 5 review)
5.MD.C.5.fullText: Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition and solve real world and mathematical problems involving volume.

5.MD.C.5.c.fullText: Recognize volume as additive; find volumes of solid figures composed of two non-overlapping right rectangular prisms.

5.OA.A.2.fullText: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them.

5.OA.B.3.fullText: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules; identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms.
